html:
NunatuKavut, "Our Ancient Land" in Inuktitut, is the homeland claimed by the Southern Inuit of central and southern Labrador, in Canada. Its people, the NunatuKavummiut, descend from Inuit who lived along this coast and from European fishermen and traders who married into their families from the 1700s.

Inuit were living on the southern Labrador coast by the 1500s or 1600s, and met Basque whalers and French fishermen in the Strait of Belle Isle, sometimes trading and sometimes fighting. Their Innu neighbours lived inland. Through the 1800s mixed families lived by fishing, sealing and trapping, under the Newfoundland government and alongside the Hudson's Bay Company. The NunatuKavut Community Council, once the Labrador Métis Nation, presses a land claim to the region; unlike Nunatsiavut to the north, it has no settled agreement.
